flags: The 2021 NCDOT guide is the route source. The cached Ashe County page reports severe September 2024 flooding in Lansing, washed-out crossings and a multiyear repair expectation; no cached DOT update establishes present byway access. Editor must resolve current access before publication; no current closure or reopening is asserted.

Material strip miles increase southward (Brandon, Lansing, Warrensville). This story explicitly drives the reverse, northbound, following NCDOT. The grave near Tuckerdale precedes the upper-corridor Pond Mountain reference; neither retained moment has coordinates, and exact stop positions are not established.

The guidebook extraction interleaves columns. Files 00–02 duplicate the beginning of the book and stop before this byway; file 16 contains the relevant printed pages 102–105 despite its URL fragment. Evidence quotes retain the extraction exactly.
Pond Mountain and the grave are deliberately short because the cache provides few usable details. No summit access, grave access or currently visible condition is promised.

The cache does not document the road’s original builders or designation campaign; the guide’s road-improvement and railroad account provides the supported transport history. The Lansing and Lansing School pages disagree on the school construction date, so that date is omitted.
